details:
Implementation Plan

Plan for #7216: before the planning model runs, close CI-repair issues whose pull request already merged with the failing check passing

Scope-mode: Hold Scope
Reuse-audit: extends files_touched_scope_guard.origin_references / fetch_issue_with_gh / _origin_author_trusted
Scope-mode justification: The answered clarification sets the scope. Q1 (derived from the repo) covers check-failure triage issues and the issues re-issued from them. Q2=A puts a check in `plan.yml`, run on the host before the model. Q3=A posts a marker comment, adds `ai:closed` and closes the issue as "not planned". Q4=A says "merged" means the PR merged and the failing check named in the triage issue passed on the PR's final head; when the check did not pass, the issue is planned against the PR's base branch. The plan does exactly that and nothing more. It does not touch PR #6976, workflow-heal issues, or how implement chooses its branch. One addition is cheap and needed for correctness, so it stays in scope (Boil the Lake; §6 puts Correctness above Speed). When the PR merged but the check did not pass, the planner gets a short fact block saying the PR merged and its head branch is not a target. Without it the planner can repeat #7185's mistake even when the checkout is already the base branch.

Automation / scheduler wiring (§20.E)
- Change type: one new helper module, `scripts/plan_superseded_merged_pr.py`. It is not a standalone or manual script: it runs only inside `plan.yml`. `plan.yml` gets one new step and two small edits.
- Entry point: `.github/workflows/plan.yml`, triggered by the existing `issue_comment` `/answer` event, through `internal-plan.yml` here and `ai-plan.yml` in consumer repos. No new trigger, cron or wrapper.
- Long-running supervisor: none.
- Database work: none.
- `docs/scripts-pending-removal.md`: no entry, because the helper is neither single-use nor long-running.

Conflicts with the issue and the answers
- The issue body (#7216) starts with "Accepted with this follow-up by the unblock judge (#7185)". `files_touched_scope_guard.ORIGIN_REFERENCE_PATTERNS` already counts that line as a source link. A lineage walk over every origin pattern would trace #7216 → #7185 → #6977 (a triage issue for PR #6976, which merged with CI green) and close #7216, a real feature request, as superseded. The walk must therefore follow only re-issue references, not follow-up references. See D2.
- The Q4 answer says "planning uses the PR's base branch instead" when the target is the old head branch. That target comes from `resolve_integration_ref.sh`, which runs before checkout (`plan.yml` "Resolve integration ref", line 123). So the reroute must re-checkout the base branch after the fact. Implement resolves its branch from the issue body on its own, and this plan does not change that (see Risks).
- `python3 -I` on Python 3.11 implies `-P`, so the script's own directory is not on `sys.path`. Like `scripts/unblock_actions.py:83`, the new module must add its own directory explicitly so it can import `files_touched_scope_guard` from the trusted support copy.

1. Files likely to change
- NEW `scripts/plan_superseded_merged_pr.py`: the classifier and its CLI.
- `.github/workflows/plan.yml`:

  - edit "Capture planning ref context" (line 965) to honour a reroute;
  - edit "Build planning context" (line 1001) to add the merged-PR fact block.
- NEW `tests/test_plan_superseded_merged_pr.py`: unit tests of the classifier with fake fetchers, including the #7185 regression.
- NEW `tests/test_plan_superseded_merged_pr_workflow.py`: workflow contract plus a behavioural run of the step body with a fake `gh` (same harness style as `tests/test_plan_template_owned_path_guard.py`).
- `.github/workflows/ci.yml`: add both test files beside `tests/test_plan_template_owned_path_guard.py` in the list near line 1266, so `tests/test_ci_wires_every_test_file.py` passes.
- `docs/INVENTORY.md`: add one line for the new script, next to `files_touched_scope_guard.py` (line 168).
- `README.md`: add a `PLAN_SUPERSEDED_MERGED_PR_CHECK_ENABLED` row to both variable tables that list `AUTOMATION_PATH_PLAN_AUTO_APPROVAL_ENABLED` (around lines 102 and 2167).
- NEW `changelog.d/7216-plan-superseded-merged-pr.md` (CLAUDE.md §20 fragment).
- NEW `agents.d/7216-plan-superseded-merged-pr.md` (§25), with two blocks:
  - `<!-- agents: section="Workflow architecture" -->`: the behaviour, in one paragraph.
  - `<!-- agents: section="Stable log prefixes (contractual)" -->`: the bullet `` - `PLAN_SUPERSEDED_MERGED_PR` (...) `` plus `LOG_PREFIX.name=PLAN_SUPERSEDED_MERGED_PR`.
- Not changed: `scripts/files_touched_scope_guard.py` (only imported), `scripts/check_failure_triage.sh`, `scripts/unblock_actions.py`, label contract, `workflow-templates/ai-plan.yml`, `agents.md`. `plan.yml` is 135,724 bytes, far under the 480,000-byte guard.

2. Functions and modules

`scripts/plan_superseded_merged_pr.py` (tabs; `from __future__ import annotations`; `sys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).resolve().parent))`, then `import files_touched_scope_guard as ftsg`):

Constants
- `REISSUE_REFERENCE_PATTERNS`: the re-issue subset of `ftsg.ORIGIN_REFERENCE_PATTERNS`, chosen by matching pattern source strings at import time, never by index:
  - `Re-issued from\s+#N` (stall recovery, no-op and validation re-issues);
  - `Re-issued by the unblock judge from #N`;
  - `^-\s*Replaces:\s*#N` (review-blocked re-issue footer).
  - Excluded: `Accepted with this follow-up…`, `- Parent issue:`, `- Source issue:` and `ai:unblock-fixup:v1`. Those mark follow-up or descoped work, not the same CI repair.
  - If any of the three source strings is missing from `ftsg`, the module raises at import, so the workflow fails open (D2).
- `TRIAGE_LABEL = "ai:check-triage"`
- `TRIAGE_PR_MARKER_RE = r"<!--\s*check-failure-triage:pr=([1-9][0-9]{0,9})\s*-->"`
- Header-line regexes, anchored `^…$` with MULTILINE and applied only to the text before the first `^---$` rule of the triage body (where `check_failure_triage.sh` lines 791–802 write the header):
  - `^- \*\*Pull request:\*\* https://github\.com/<owner>/<repo>/pull/(N) \(`[^`]*`\)$`, with owner/repo required to equal `--repo` (case-insensitive);
  - `^- \*\*Failing check:\*\* `([^`]{1,200})` \(conclusion: `[^`]*`\)$`;
  - optional `^- \*\*Check run id:\*\* `([0-9]+)`$`;
  - `^- \*\*Check details:\*\* (https://github\.com/<owner>/<repo>/actions/runs/([0-9]+)\S*)$` (needed only for workflow-run triage).
- `BRANCH_RE = ^[A-Za-z0-9._/-]{1,200}$`, rejecting any name containing `..`.
- `SHA_RE = ^[0-9a-f]{40}$`

Functions
- `reissue_references(body) -> list[int]`: matches `REISSUE_REFERENCE_PATTERNS` only. Reuses `ftsg.origin_references`'s unnamed-footer check: if `origin_references(body)[1]` is true, the result is `origin_unverified`.
- `parse_triage_source(meta, repo, pipeline_login) -> dict | None`: returns `{pr, check_name, check_run_id|None, details_run_id|None}` only when all of these hold:
  - the issue carries `ai:check-triage`;
  - `ftsg._origin_author_trusted(meta, login)[0]` is true;
  - the Pull request and Failing check lines parse;
  - the marker's `pr=` equals the Pull request line's number;
  - for workflow-run triage (no check-run id), the details URL parses.
- `is_candidate(meta) -> bool`: an API-free pre-filter. True when the issue has the triage label, or its body matches any `REISSUE_REFERENCE_PATTERNS`. Everything else returns early with no API call.
- `resolve_source(meta, repo, pipeline_login, fetch) -> (status, source|None, issues_read)`:
  - Direct: return the parsed triage source when the issue qualifies itself.
  - Lineage: allowed only when the issue author is the pipeline login. Walk breadth-first over `reissue_references`, bounded by `ftsg.ORIGIN_MAX_DEPTH` and `ftsg.ORIGIN_MAX_ISSUES`, using `fetch` (default `ftsg.fetch_issue_with_gh`). At each node:
    - an untrusted author ends the walk with `untrusted_origin`;
    - a direct triage source is recorded;
    - a pipeline-authored node is walked further;
    - a trusted human non-triage node ends that branch.
  - A failed read, an exceeded bound or an unnamed footer gives `origin_unverified`.
  - More than one distinct `(pr, check_name)` source gives `ambiguous_source`.
  - Status is `ok` or `no_source` otherwise.
- `pr_state(repo, pr, gh) -> dict`: one `gh api repos/<repo>/pulls/<N>` read. Returns:
  - `merged` (true when `merged_at` is set);
  - `state`;
  - `head_sha` (must match `SHA_RE`);
  - `head_ref` and `base_ref` (must match `BRANCH_RE`);
  - `head_repo`.
- `check_passed_on(repo, source, head_sha, gh) -> "success"|"failed"|"pending"|"unknown"`:
  - Check-run triage: `gh api -X GET repos/<repo>/commits/<sha>/check-runs -f check_name=<name> -f filter=latest -f per_page=100`. Uses the same predicate as `check_failure_triage.sh` lines 474–476: success only when the list is non-empty, `total_count <= len`, and every run is completed with conclusion `success`.
  - Workflow-run triage:
    1. `gh api repos/<repo>/actions/runs/<details_run_id>`; require `repository.full_name == repo` and a numeric `workflow_id`.
    2. `gh api "repos/<repo>/actions/workflows/<wid>/runs?head_sha=<sha>&per_page=1"`; success only when `workflow_runs[0]` exists with `status=completed` and `conclusion=success`.
  - Any read or parse failure returns `unknown`.
- `classify(meta, repo, pipeline_login, fetch, gh) -> dict` returns one JSON object with:
  - `outcome`: `superseded` | `merged_check_not_passed` | `plan`;
  - `reason`; `source_issue`; `pr`; `base_ref`; `head_ref`; `final_head_sha`; `check_name`; `check_result`; `issues_read`; `api_calls`.

  Reason by case:

  | Case | Outcome | Reason |
  |---|---|---|
  | No triage source found | `plan` | `not_candidate`, `no_source`, `origin_unverified`, `untrusted_orig
